:::{#exm-surprisal-uniform}
#### Surprisal of a value of a uniform random variable

Let $X$ be [uniformly distributed](random-variables.qmd#def-uniform) on the interval from $0$ to $a > 0$,
so that its [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) is $\p(X=x) = 1/a$ for $0 < x < a$.
Every value in the interval has [surprisal](#def-surprisal-continuous)

$$\surprisalf{x} = -\log \tfrac{1}{a} = \log a.$$

With $a = \tfrac{1}{2}$ and logarithms to base 2, the surprisal of every value is $\log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} = -1$ bit.
A density value can exceed $1$,
so unlike the surprisal of a [discrete](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) value, it can be negative.
